ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Ernest Hemingway

code.originalText: Two-week review with the hepatology consultation: HFE result, liver stiffness and the phlebotomy plan

text.paragraph: Two-week review, seen the same day by hepatology. [S]

Mr. Hemingway returns two weeks after intake and is seen by Dr. Solheim of hepatology on the same day. The HFE test drawn at intake shows that he is homozygous for C282Y. He has taken naltrexone 50 mg daily; he had mild nausea for three days, which passed. By his diary he has cut down from about ten drinks a day to five or six, with none before evening on most days. He has had no tremor, sweats or trouble sleeping beyond his usual. He has taken sertraline 50 mg daily with loose stools for a few days and no other side effects. His home blood pressure average is 146/90 on amlodipine 5 mg. His guns were taken to the locked storage at his shooting club the week after intake, and he keeps no ammunition at home. He has started weekly psychotherapy. His headaches are unchanged, two or three a week. [S]

list.item:
Hereditary hemochromatosis, C282Y homozygous (E83.110). C282Y homozygosity with a transferrin saturation of 76% and a ferritin over 1,000 ng/mL confirms hereditary hemochromatosis with iron overload. Because the ferritin is over 1,000 ng/mL and the ALT is raised, the liver must be staged. Dr. Solheim's elastography today is indeterminate at 9.4 kPa, which recent drinking may raise, so an MRI with liver iron quantification and elastography is planned instead of a biopsy. [S]
Weekly phlebotomy of 500 mL from next week, with a hemoglobin check before each session.
MRI of the liver with iron quantification and elastography.
No iron or vitamin C supplements; no raw shellfish.
A letter explaining HFE testing for first-degree relatives, which he may share as he chooses.

Alcohol use disorder, severe, on naltrexone (F10.20). Halved his drinking in two weeks on naltrexone, without withdrawal symptoms. Dr. Solheim advised that alcohol and iron overload together greatly raise the risk of cirrhosis, and that stopping would be best for his liver. He wants to keep cutting down first and decide about stopping when the MRI is back. Liver tests are falling. [S]
Continue naltrexone 50 mg daily and thiamine 100 mg daily.
Reduce by about one drink a day each week; call for tremor, sweating, racing heart or confusion.

Depression (F32.1). Two weeks on sertraline 50 mg with minor side effects. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or wishes to be dead since the last visit; firearms stored off-site; the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline in his phone. [S]
Continue sertraline 50 mg daily.
Weekly psychotherapy.

Hypertension (I10). Home average 146/90 after two weeks on amlodipine 5 mg and less alcohol; too early to judge the full effect. [S]
Continue amlodipine 5 mg daily and home readings.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Diagnosis and management of hemochromatosis: 2011 practice guideline by the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (2011); ACG Clinical Guideline: Hereditary Hemochromatosis (2019); The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Pharmacological Treatment of Patients With Alcohol Use Disorder (2018); The ASAM Clinical Practice Guideline on Alcohol Withdrawal Management (2020); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Major Depressive Disorder (2022); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension and depression, bipolar, and mood disorders monographs (2026)

Follow-up: Weekly phlebotomy from next week. MRI of the liver within four weeks. Six-week review in four weeks with blood count, ferritin, liver tests, PHQ-9 and AUDIT-C. Weekly psychotherapy.
